messages.author: 97631c37e94d1a09
messages.subject: Calibration data
parts: Sorry if this question is covered somewhere obvious. I have inherited some Argos doppler and GPS data that I am using for a spatial analysis on Clark's nutcrackers (bird). To my knowledge, no calibration was performed for the transmitters before they were deployed. For the GPS data, I have the fix type (2D or 3D) and for the Doppler data, I have the error ellipse information, including GDOP values (in mHz). Can I perform any kind of opportunistic calibration using these values, other values provided by Argos that I have not listed, or calibration data from an unrelated project as a better-than-nothing measure? Thanks in advance, I am very new to spatial analysis and can use all the help I can get.

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Calibration data
parts:
Hi Karina,

Sorry for the delay.

The Argos error ellipses don't need to be calibrated.

If you need to calibrate the GPS errors, then yes, you can. However, if the sampling rate is not very high, then it might be safe to ignore the GPS location error (but not the Argos location error).

Best,
Chris
